newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on low volume.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on low volume.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, on lows volumes, as the metals market wound down for the Christmas and New Year holidays.
"The day was featureless, apart from a little more year end fund shortcovering and position squaring ahead of the holidays," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
COMEX February gold ended down 60 cents at $370.50, after trading in a narrow $371.40-370.20 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 15,000 lots.
"February gold could remained trapped in its $367-$380 range during the holiday period," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted around $368.30/80, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $369.00 and the New York close Thursday at $369.00/50.
COMEX March silver ended down 2.7 cent at $4.858, well off its session high at $4.935. Estimated total silver volume was 10,000 lots.
The monthly precious metals OTC option expiry went off without creating any volatility, and US third quarter GDP showed a rise of 2.1 pct, within expectations.
In the past two weeks, the precious metals complex has been consolidating or recovering partially from the year's lows seen in late November.

But the latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data, for the week ended December 17, released after the market closed Friday, showed only a limited decrease in net short open interest by funds in most of the complex, analysts noted.
NYMEX January platinum closed up $1.50 at $375.30, while NYMEX March palladium ended up 20 cents at $121.15.

Platinum group metals received some support from news of progess in passing the Russian budget, which may remove some of the need for extra Russian sales of platinum and palladium in the spot market, traders said.
